knowledge_base.name: Oracle 19c Legacy Code Assistant Knowledge Base
knowledge_base.description: Curated diagnostic references for Oracle Database 19c, grounded in official Oracle documentation. Community reports are secondary diagnostic leads, not proof of Oracle defects.

issues.title: Oracle Streams desupported in 19c
symptoms: code references DBMS_STREAMS, DBMS_CAPTURE, DBMS_APPLY, DBMS_PROPAGATION
Streams-based replication no longer functional after upgrade
issues.rule: Oracle Streams is desupported in Oracle Database 19c. Code that references Streams packages will not work.
issues.replacement: Oracle GoldenGate for real-time replication; XStream for programmatic change capture.
diagnostic_steps: Search codebase for DBMS_STREAMS, DBMS_CAPTURE, DBMS_APPLY, DBMS_PROPAGATION references.
Identify whether the code uses Streams for replication, CDC, or messaging.
Plan migration to GoldenGate or XStream based on use case.
recommended_actions: Replace Oracle Streams with Oracle GoldenGate.
For lightweight CDC, evaluate Oracle XStream API.

confidence.meaning: Confirmed desupported by Oracle upgrade documentation.

issues.title: CONTINUOUS_MINE option desupported in 19c
symptoms: DBMS_LOGMNR.START_LOGMNR call with CONTINUOUS_MINE fails
LogMiner-based CDC no longer mines online redo logs continuously
issues.rule: The CONTINUOUS_MINE option of DBMS_LOGMNR.START_LOGMNR is desupported in 19c. LogMiner still works for offline analysis, but continuous redo mining requires alternatives.
issues.replacement: Use Oracle GoldenGate or XStream for continuous change capture. LogMiner remains available for offline redo log analysis.
diagnostic_steps: Check if code passes CONTINUOUS_MINE option to DBMS_LOGMNR.START_LOGMNR.
Determine if continuous CDC is required or if batch analysis suffices.
recommended_actions: Remove CONTINUOUS_MINE and switch to GoldenGate for real-time CDC.
If batch is acceptable, continue using LogMiner with explicit log file registration.

confidence.meaning: Confirmed desupported by Oracle upgrade documentation.

issues.title: PRODUCT_USER_PROFILE table desupported in 19c
symptoms: SQL*Plus product-level security using PRODUCT_USER_PROFILE no longer enforced
references to SYSTEM.PRODUCT_USER_PROFILE in scripts
issues.rule: The SQL*Plus PRODUCT_USER_PROFILE table is desupported. Product-level security restrictions based on this table are no longer enforced.
issues.replacement: Use Oracle Database Vault, VPD, or standard GRANT/REVOKE privileges for access control.
diagnostic_steps: Search for references to PRODUCT_USER_PROFILE in deployment scripts and SQL*Plus startup files.
Identify what restrictions were enforced via this mechanism.
recommended_actions: Remove references to PRODUCT_USER_PROFILE.
Implement equivalent restrictions using database privileges or Database Vault.

confidence.meaning: Confirmed desupported by Oracle upgrade documentation.

issues.title: Oracle Multimedia desupported in 19c
symptoms: code references ORDImage, ORDAudio, ORDVideo, ORDDoc types
Oracle Multimedia PL/SQL packages no longer available after upgrade
issues.rule: Oracle Multimedia (formerly Oracle interMedia) is desupported in 19c. All ORDSYS types and packages are removed.
issues.replacement: Store media as BLOBs with application-layer processing. Use third-party libraries for image/audio/video handling.
diagnostic_steps: Search for ORDSYS, ORDImage, ORDAudio, ORDVideo, ORDDoc in schema and code.
Identify columns using Oracle Multimedia types.
recommended_actions: Migrate Oracle Multimedia columns to BLOB.
Move media processing to the application tier.

confidence.meaning: Confirmed desupported by Oracle upgrade documentation.

issues.title: DBMS_JOB deprecated — use DBMS_SCHEDULER
symptoms: legacy scheduled jobs use DBMS_JOB.SUBMIT or DBMS_JOB.CHANGE
job scheduling code predates Oracle 10g Scheduler
issues.rule: DBMS_JOB is deprecated. It still functions in 19c but may be desupported in a future release. New jobs should use DBMS_SCHEDULER.
issues.replacement: DBMS_SCHEDULER provides richer scheduling, logging, chaining, and resource management.
diagnostic_steps: Search for DBMS_JOB references in PL/SQL code and deployment scripts.
Inventory existing DBMS_JOB entries via DBA_JOBS view.
recommended_actions: Migrate existing jobs to DBMS_SCHEDULER.
Use DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB for new scheduled tasks.

confidence.meaning: Deprecated per Oracle documentation; still functional but flagged for future removal.

issues.title: DBMS_XMLQUERY and DBMS_XMLSAVE deprecated
symptoms: code uses DBMS_XMLQUERY.GETXML or DBMS_XMLSAVE
XML generation or DML through deprecated XML packages
issues.rule: DBMS_XMLQUERY and DBMS_XMLSAVE are deprecated. Use XMLTABLE, XMLQUERY, XMLType methods, or DBMS_XMLGEN.
issues.replacement: DBMS_XMLGEN for query-to-XML. XMLTABLE for XML-to-relational. XMLType methods for manipulation.
diagnostic_steps: Search for DBMS_XMLQUERY and DBMS_XMLSAVE calls.
Determine if the code generates XML from queries or performs XML-based DML.
recommended_actions: Replace DBMS_XMLQUERY with DBMS_XMLGEN or SQL/XML functions.
Replace DBMS_XMLSAVE with standard DML using XMLTABLE.

confidence.meaning: Deprecated per Oracle PL/SQL Packages and Types Reference.

issues.title: TO_DATE without format mask — NLS dependency
symptoms: TO_DATE fails with ORA-01858 or ORA-01843 after migration
date conversion works in one environment but fails in another
implicit NLS_DATE_FORMAT dependency
issues.rule: TO_DATE called with only one argument relies on the session NLS_DATE_FORMAT. This is a portability hazard; always supply an explicit format mask.
diagnostic_steps: Check TO_DATE calls for missing format mask argument.
Compare NLS_DATE_FORMAT between source and target environments.
recommended_actions: Add explicit format mask: TO_DATE('2024-01-15', 'YYYY-MM-DD').
Use ANSI date literals where appropriate: DATE '2024-01-15'.

confidence.meaning: Documented NLS behavior; a well-known migration pitfall.

issues.title: Implicit VARCHAR2-to-NUMBER conversion in predicates
symptoms: ORA-01722: invalid number
query performance degradation due to full table scan where index was expected
predicate comparing VARCHAR2 column to a number literal
issues.rule: When Oracle compares a VARCHAR2 column to a NUMBER, it converts the column values to NUMBER, which prevents index usage and can raise ORA-01722 if the column contains non-numeric data.
diagnostic_steps: Identify predicates where a VARCHAR2 column is compared to a numeric literal.
Check if the column data contains any non-numeric values.
Review the execution plan for unexpected full table scans.
recommended_actions: Use TO_CHAR on the numeric side: WHERE varchar_col = TO_CHAR(123).
Or convert the column type if it genuinely holds only numbers.

issues.title: SELECT * fragility in production code
symptoms: application breaks after a column is added to or removed from a table
PL/SQL %ROWTYPE variables pick up unexpected columns
issues.rule: SELECT * in production code is fragile. Schema changes (added, removed, or reordered columns) silently alter the result set, potentially breaking callers.
diagnostic_steps: Identify SELECT * usage in production SQL and PL/SQL.
Determine if callers depend on column position or count.
recommended_actions: Replace SELECT * with an explicit column list.
Use %ROWTYPE only when intentionally accepting all columns.

issues.title: ORA-28040 — authentication protocol mismatch after upgrade
symptoms: ORA-28040: No matching authentication protocol
client cannot connect after database upgrade to 19c
older JDBC drivers or Oracle clients fail authentication
issues.rule: Oracle 19c defaults SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER to 12, requiring SHA-1 (11G) or SHA-512 (12C) password verifiers. Clients using the 10G protocol or older will fail with ORA-28040.
diagnostic_steps: Check SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER in sqlnet.ora.
Verify the client/driver version supports the required authentication protocol.
Check DBA_USERS.PASSWORD_VERSIONS for the accounts in question.
recommended_actions: Upgrade JDBC drivers and Oracle clients to versions compatible with 19c.
If legacy client upgrade is not possible, consult Oracle Security Guide for SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER adjustment (security trade-off).
Reset affected user passwords after adjusting allowed logon versions to generate correct verifiers.
do_not: Do not blindly lower SQLNET.ALLOWED_LOGON_VERSION_SERVER without understanding the security implications.
Do not recommend disabling password verifier checks as a general fix.

confidence.meaning: Documented default change in Oracle 19c security configuration.

sources.section: Configuring Authentication — Oracle Database Security Guide

issues.title: SQL Macros — new in 19c, replaces views and functions for performance
symptoms: complex views causing optimizer barriers
scalar PL/SQL functions called per-row causing context switches
issues.rule: Oracle 19c introduces SQL Macros (scalar and table). They inline at parse time, avoiding PL/SQL-to-SQL context switches and enabling better optimizer plans.
diagnostic_steps: Identify scalar PL/SQL functions called in SQL that cause per-row context switches.
Check if the function logic can be expressed as a SQL expression.
recommended_actions: For new code, use SQL_MACRO(SCALAR) to define inline expressions.
For existing views causing optimizer barriers, consider SQL_MACRO(TABLE).

confidence.meaning: New feature documented in Oracle 19c SQL Language Reference.

issues.title: IF [NOT] EXISTS DDL syntax — new in 19c
symptoms: deployment scripts use EXECUTE IMMEDIATE with exception handlers for DDL idempotency
scripts wrap CREATE/DROP in PL/SQL blocks to suppress ORA-00955 or ORA-00942
issues.rule: Oracle 19c supports IF [NOT] EXISTS on CREATE and DROP statements, eliminating the need for PL/SQL exception-swallowing wrappers in deployment scripts.
diagnostic_steps: Search for PL/SQL blocks that wrap CREATE/DROP TABLE in BEGIN...EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS...END.
Identify if the exception handling exists solely for DDL idempotency.
recommended_actions: Replace PL/SQL wrappers with: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ... or DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ...
Simplify deployment and migration scripts.

confidence.meaning: New DDL syntax documented in Oracle 19c SQL Language Reference.

issues.title: Unguarded WHEN OTHERS exception handler swallows errors
symptoms: errors silently ignored in PL/SQL
data corruption from swallowed exceptions
WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL pattern
issues.rule: A WHEN OTHERS handler that does not re-raise (RAISE) or log to a persistent table silently swallows errors. This is the most common PL/SQL anti-pattern and a frequent source of data corruption in legacy code.
diagnostic_steps: Search for WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL or WHEN OTHERS without RAISE.
Determine if the handler logs to a persistent audit/error table.
Check if the handler is intentionally suppressing a specific expected error.
recommended_actions: Add RAISE at the end of WHEN OTHERS handlers to re-propagate unexpected errors.
If suppression is intentional, use a specific exception handler (e.g., WHEN NO_DATA_FOUND) instead.
Log error details with DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK and FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE.

confidence.meaning: Well-documented PL/SQL best practice in Oracle PL/SQL Language Reference.

issues.title: Row-by-row processing instead of BULK COLLECT / FORALL
symptoms: cursor loop with single-row FETCH
INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE inside a cursor FOR loop
slow PL/SQL execution with high context switch overhead
issues.rule: Row-by-row processing in PL/SQL causes excessive SQL-to-PL/SQL context switches. BULK COLLECT with FORALL reduces context switches dramatically.
diagnostic_steps: Identify cursor FOR loops that perform DML inside the loop body.
Check if BULK COLLECT with LIMIT is used for large result sets.
Measure V$SESSTAT 'SQL*Net roundtrips' before and after conversion.
recommended_actions: Convert single-row FETCH loops to BULK COLLECT with a LIMIT clause.
Use FORALL for batch DML instead of row-by-row INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.
Consider a pure SQL solution (MERGE, INSERT...SELECT) when possible.

confidence.meaning: Documented Oracle PL/SQL performance best practice.

issues.title: Invalid multi-part column reference after migration
symptoms: invalid identifier
query fails after migration
issues.rule: A community report of ORA-00904 after migration. Not evidence of a 19c regression — investigate the specific SQL identifiers.
diagnostic_steps: Inspect the FROM clause and verify table aliases.
Check whether the referenced column exists in the intended table.
Verify alias usage does not include an extra qualifier.
recommended_actions: Correct the identifier reference based on actual schema.
If schema is unavailable, ask the developer to verify.

confidence.meaning: A reported example; not official confirmation of a 19c defect.

issues.title: Query behavior differs after migration — optimizer investigation needed
symptoms: query returns different results after migration to 19c
unexpected empty result set
issues.rule: A community report of differing query results after 12c-to-19c migration. Requires execution plan comparison and environment investigation.
diagnostic_steps: Reproduce with same data, bind values, and session settings.
Compare execution plans between environments.
Check the exact 19c release update and patch level.
recommended_actions: Collect evidence before changing SQL or optimizer parameters.
If confirmed, search Oracle support for matching symptoms.

confidence.meaning: Reported behavior; root cause requires independent verification.
